title: refactor(tf): unify GPU topology module and migrate tfstate layout for tenant-scoped roles
author: Arjun Patel
description:
Context and motivation: Private deployments have diverged in how GPU node pools, IAM scoping, and subnet affinity are expressed across Terraform modules. That divergence complicates upgrades and has led to several manual tfstate fixes during tenant onboarding. This PR introduces a single 'gpu_topology' Terraform module that expresses node pool topology, AZ-aware subnet affinity, and scoped IAM role attachments. Alongside the module refactor we are migrating the tfstate layout to 'v2' which encodes tenant-scoped namespaces and reduces the number of remote state backends required per cluster. The migration is assisted by a new idempotent migrator script (scripts/tfstate-migrator/migrate_v1_to_v2.py) and an interactive dry-run mode.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds modules/gpu-topology: unified module to declare GPU pools, AZ distribution, taints/affinity, and pool-level IAM bindings.
- Refactors modules/iam to expose tenant-scoped role templates and a minimal binding shim consumed by gpu-topology.
- Reworks modules/networking to add optional subnetClaim inputs for per-pool affinity and to emit stable subnet identifiers used by the migrator.
- Introduces a tfstate layout v2 (terraform/state/layout_v2.md) and a migrator to move existing state entries into the new namespaced keys.
- Adds examples/tenant-cluster/gpu-topology.tf showing the new module usage and upgrade steps.

Design notes and compatibility: The new gpu_topology module keeps backward compatibility at the resource level where possible: the underlying resources (node pools, routes, IAM policies) remain the same names where feasible, but their Terraform resource addresses change when a tenant namespace is added. To avoid drift we do not touch existing provider configuration or TF backend settings; instead the migrator rewrites remote state entries and performs a controlled import where needed. The migrator supports a dry-run and a 'checkpoint' mode that emits a manifest of moved addresses for manual verification.

Migration and rollout plan (required):
1) Run terraform plan in a non-prod tenant with the 'tfstate-migrator --dry-run' and review manifest. (Linear: ENG-2145)
2) Run the migrator in checkpoint mode and validate imports in the target workspace.
3) Apply the updated terraform modules in canary tenants (we have provided examples/ and a smoke test in tests/terraform-canary/).
4) Monitor the rollout via Console dashboards and the new 'tfstate-migration' CloudWatch metrics/alerts (observability changes included).
5) If migration must be reverted, the migrator supports a rollback manifest to reconstruct previous keys; see rollback instructions in docs/upgrade.md.

Testing performed: unit tests for module input validation (modules/gpu-topology/test/), full integration in our perf-canary environment, and migration dry-runs against snapshot state from three tenants. CI: terraform fmt/lint, tflint rules, and the migrator python tests were re-run; CI initially failed on a linter rule (resource naming) and was fixed in the second commit.

Security and IAM considerations: tenant-scoped roles are created with least privilege templates. We audited IAM ARNs and removed an overly-broad write role previously granted at the project level. The change requires a brief maintenance window for large tenants (~10-15 minutes) during the migration; documented in the release notes.

Rollback: the migrator emits a reversible manifest and an automated rollback command. In addition the PR includes a short playbook (docs/upgrade.md -> 'Rollback' section) for manual steps if the automated path fails.

Related work: follows on from previous state cleanup efforts (see ENG-1970) and pairs with a future change to the private-installer chart to expose gpu pool selectors (planned in INFRA-309).
commits: module(gpu_topology): introduce unified topology module (initial API)
tfstate: add v2 layout specification and migrator tool (migrate_v1_to_v2)
modules/iam: add tenant-scoped role template and minimal binding shim
networking: expose subnet_claim inputs used by gpu_topology
examples: add tenant-cluster/gpu-topology example and smoke test
tests: add terraform canary integration and migrator unit tests
fix(lint): resource naming and tflint fixes after review
review_comments: Sofie Martinez: Please add an explicit acceptance test that simulates a mid-size tenant (1000 pods) to validate the migration window. Reply (Arjun Patel): Added a lightweight smoke test under tests/terraform-canary and documented expected timings in docs/upgrade.md.

Luca Romano: The migrator currently assumes the remote backend supports state mv operations; can we support backends without state mv? Reply (Arjun Patel): Migrator now includes an import-based fallback (flag --use-import) that reconstructs resources in the target namespace when state mv isn't supported.

Jamie Cole: We should not change IAM bindings in-place during migration to avoid transient permission gaps. Suggest create-then-swap approach. Reply (Arjun Patel): Implemented create-then-swap pattern in modules/iam and added a 60s stabilization pause configurable via variable 'iam_binding_swap_delay'.
release_notes: Summary: Introduces a unified GPU topology Terraform module and a tfstate layout v2 with a supported migrator. Impact: tfstate keys will be namespaced per-tenant; a migration step is required for existing private installs. Migration: use scripts/tfstate-migrator/migrate_v1_to_v2.py --dry-run; then run with --checkpoint to perform the move. Testing: run tests/terraform-canary against a canary tenant before full rollout. Rollback: migrator emits a rollback manifest; see docs/upgrade.md for manual steps. Operational note: expect a maintenance window for large tenants (10-15 minutes).
